pages.title: The First Human
pages.content:
A very long time ago, Allah made the sky and the earth. Then He told the angels about a new person. This person was going to live on the earth. The angels were surprised.

The angels took soil from many parts of the earth. Allah made the first human from this soil. His name was Adam. Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) told us about this soil. It came from many different places. Because of this, people have different skin colors. Adam is the father of all people. We are all his children.

vocabulary.definition: The world we live on.
A being of light; it always does what Allah says.
Feeling "Oh! I did not know that!".
The brown ground; plants grow in it.

hotspots.title: The Angels
hotspots.description: Allah told the angels about a new person. The angels were surprised.

hotspots.title: Soil from Many Places
hotspots.description: The soil came from many places. Because of this, people have different skin colors.

exercises.title: The First Human
exercises.instructions: Read. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: What happened in Chapter 1?

items: The angels took soil from many parts of the earth.
Adam is the father of all people.
The angels made the first human.

True: The angels took soil from many parts of the earth.
Adam is the father of all people.
False: The angels made the first human.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 1 says: “Allah made the first human from this soil.” The angels only took the soil.

feedback.correct: Yes! Allah made Adam. The angels took the soil.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Made, Took, Told
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match the verb with its past form.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the past form?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: The story happened a long time ago, so it is in the past. These verbs change in the past: made, took, told, came.

feedback.correct: Good. You found the past forms.
feedback.incorrect: Find made, took, told and came in Chapter 1.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: A Long Time Ago
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Which words tell the past?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Allah [blank] the sky and the earth. The angels [blank] soil from many parts of the earth. His name [blank] Adam.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: All three sentences tell the past. We use made, took and was.

feedback.correct: Correct. All three words tell the past.
feedback.incorrect: Look at Chapter 1. Find made, took and was.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: All People
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say three sentences about Chapter 1.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do you know about Adam?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use the facts from Chapter 1 only.

feedback.correct: Say one thing in each sentence.

discussionPrompts.question: “Allah made Adam from …”
discussionPrompts.example: Allah made Adam from soil.

discussionPrompts.question: “Adam is the father of …”
discussionPrompts.example: Adam is the father of all people.

discussionPrompts.question: “People have different …”
discussionPrompts.example: People have different skin colors.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Allah make the first human from?
beforeYouRead.quote: Allah made the first human from this soil.

iCan: I can say what Allah made Adam from.
I can use made, took and told.
I can say why people have different skin colors.

pages.title: Iblis Says No
pages.content:
Allah gave Adam knowledge. Adam could learn, think and understand. Allah taught him the names of many things. Adam knew more than the angels. Allah told the angels to show respect to Adam. All the angels did this. But Iblis did not.

Allah asked Iblis about this. Iblis said, “I am better than Adam. You made me from fire, and You made Adam from soil.” He thought he was too important. He did not say sorry to Allah. So, Allah told Iblis, “Get out of here!” Iblis was wrong.

vocabulary.definition: The things you know and learn.
A feeling that someone is important.
Something very hot, red and yellow.

hotspots.title: Knowledge
hotspots.description: Allah taught Adam the names of many things. Adam could learn, think and understand.

hotspots.title: Iblis Says No
hotspots.description: Iblis said, “I am better than Adam.” He did not show respect to Adam.

exercises.title: Why Did Iblis Say No?
exercises.question: Why did Iblis not show respect to Adam?
options: Iblis thought he was better than Adam.
exercises.explanation: Iblis said, “I am better than Adam. You made me from fire, and You made Adam from soil.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Iblis thought he was better.
feedback.incorrect: Read what Iblis said in Chapter 2.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Could
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the right answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: “Adam could learn, think and understand.” What is “could”?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Could” is the past of “can”. Today: I can read. In the past: I could read.

feedback.correct: Yes. Could = can, in the past.
feedback.incorrect: Read the sentence again: “Adam could learn, think and understand.”

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Did or Did Not?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the right words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who did it? Who did not?

formChoices.sentence: All the angels [choice] respect to Adam.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: For “no” in the past, we use did not + verb: did not show, did not say.

feedback.correct: Correct. Did not + verb.
feedback.incorrect: Look at Chapter 2. Did Iblis show respect? Did he say sorry?

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: I Could
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say what you could do as a child.
languageFocusExercises.question: What could you do when you were five?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use could and could not + verb.

feedback.correct: Say one could sentence and one could not sentence.

discussionPrompts.question: “When I was five, I could …”
discussionPrompts.example: When I was five, I could swim.

discussionPrompts.question: “When I was five, I could not …”
discussionPrompts.example: When I was five, I could not read.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Who did not show respect to Adam?
beforeYouRead.quote: All the angels did this. But Iblis did not.

iCan: I can say why Iblis did not show respect.
I can use could.
I can use did not in the past.

pages.title: A Beautiful Garden
pages.content:
Iblis was very angry. He hated Adam. He wanted Adam to be sad, too. Allah told Adam to be careful. Iblis was not his friend.

Adam lived in Paradise. It was a very beautiful garden. But Adam had no one with him. Then Allah gave him a wife. Her name was Eve (Hawwa). Everything in Paradise was for them. Allah told them only one thing: “Do not go near this tree.”

vocabulary.definition: Very unhappy because of something bad.
Thinking before you do something.
Allah's beautiful garden; Jannah.

hotspots.title: Paradise
hotspots.description: Adam lived in Paradise. It was a very beautiful garden.

hotspots.title: One Tree
hotspots.description: Allah told Adam and Eve, “Do not go near this tree.”

exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Allah told Adam to be careful.
Allah told them, “Do not go near this tree.”

exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: Iblis was angry. Allah told Adam to be careful. Then Allah gave Adam a wife, Eve. Allah told them one thing.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapter 3 from the start again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Was or Were?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each sentence in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: One or many?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: One person or thing: was. Two or more: were.

feedback.correct: Good. One: was. Two or more: were.
feedback.incorrect: Is it one person or thing, or two or more?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Do Not

languageFocusExercises.question: What did Allah tell them?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Do not” + verb tells a person not to do something. “Be careful” is a short and important sentence.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use is, there are and do not.

discussionPrompts.example: My mother’s garden is a beautiful place.

discussionPrompts.question: “There are … there.”
discussionPrompts.example: There are many trees and flowers there.

discussionPrompts.question: “Do not … there.”

beforeYouRead.question: Look at the picture. Where did Adam live?
beforeYouRead.quote: It was a very beautiful garden.

I can use was and were.

groupTask.title: The Garden Poster
steps: The group draws a big garden on a poster.

pages.title: A Big Mistake
pages.content:
One day, Iblis came to Adam and Eve. He said, “I am your friend. Eat from that tree, and you will never die.” It was a big lie. After some time, Adam and Eve believed him. They forgot Allah’s words. They ate fruit from the tree. Sadly, sometimes people forget and make mistakes.

Adam and Eve were very sad. They knew it was a mistake. They said sorry to Allah, and Allah forgave them. Iblis was different. He never said sorry. He always thought he was right. Iblis did not see the right way. He thought he was too important.

vocabulary.definition: Words that are not true.
Think that something is true.
Something wrong that you do.
Stop being angry with someone.

hotspots.description: Iblis said, “I am your friend.” It was not true. It was a big lie.

exercises.title: A Big Mistake
exercises.instructions: Read. Is it true or false?
exercises.question: What happened in Chapter 4?

items: Adam and Eve ate fruit from the tree.

True: Adam and Eve ate fruit from the tree.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 4 says: “They ate fruit from the tree.” “Allah forgave them.” “He never said sorry.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Adam and Eve said sorry. Iblis never said sorry.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Past Forms
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Match the verb with its past form.
languageFocusExercises.question: What is the past form?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: These verbs change in the past. They do not end in -ed.

feedback.correct: Good. You found the past forms.
feedback.incorrect: Find ate, forgot, knew and forgave in Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Always or Never?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose always or never.
languageFocusExercises.question: Every time or not one time?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Always = every time. Never = not one time.

feedback.correct: Correct. Iblis never said sorry. He always thought he was right.
feedback.incorrect: Read the last two sentences of Chapter 4.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Sorry
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say what you do after a mistake.
languageFocusExercises.question: What do you do after a mistake?

feedback.correct: Say two sentences: one with always and one with never.

discussionPrompts.question: “After a mistake, I always …”
discussionPrompts.example: After a mistake, I always say sorry.

discussionPrompts.question: “I never …”
discussionPrompts.example: I never tell lies.

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Iblis tell Adam and Eve?

iCan: I can say what Adam and Eve did after their mistake.
I can use ate, knew and forgave.
I can use always and never.

pages.title: Life on Earth
pages.content:
Then Allah sent Adam and Eve to the earth. They worked on farms and grew food. They had animals and made houses. They looked after plants and animals, and they helped people in need. But Iblis came to the earth, too. He wanted people to forget Allah.

Adam and Eve had many children. Allah made Adam His first Messenger. Adam taught his children to be good and honest. He told them to remember Allah. He also told them, “Iblis is not your friend. Be careful.”

vocabulary.definition: Make plants come up from the soil.
A person who brings Allah's words.
Always says true things.

hotspots.title: Work on the Farm
hotspots.description: Adam and Eve worked on farms and grew food. They had animals and made houses.

hotspots.title: The First Messenger
hotspots.description: Allah made Adam His first Messenger.

exercises.question: What did Adam tell his children?

exercises.explanation: Chapter 5 says: “Adam taught his children to be good and honest. He told them to remember Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Be good and honest, and remember Allah.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Verbs with -ed
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
languageFocusExercises.question: Does the verb end in -ed?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed in the past: work → worked, help → helped. Some verbs change: grow → grew, teach → taught.

feedback.correct: Good. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: work, grow … Does it add -ed or change?

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Life on Earth

languageFocusExercises.question: What did Adam and Eve do?
languageFocusExercises.fillBlanksText: Adam and Eve [blank] on farms. They [blank] after plants and animals. They [blank] people in need.

feedback.correct: Correct. Worked, looked and helped.
feedback.incorrect: Look at the first paragraph of Chapter 5.

languageFocusExercises.title: Say It: Helping at Home
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Say how you helped at home yesterday.
languageFocusExercises.question: How did you help yesterday?
languageFocusExercises.explanation: Use past verbs with -ed.

feedback.correct: Say three sentences with -ed verbs.

discussionPrompts.question: “Yesterday, I helped …”
discussionPrompts.example: Yesterday, I helped my father.

discussionPrompts.question: “I looked after …”

discussionPrompts.question: “I worked …”

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: What did Adam and Eve do on the earth?
beforeYouRead.quote: They worked on farms and grew food.

iCan: I can say how Adam and Eve lived on the earth.

pages.title: Two Brothers
pages.content:
Adam and Eve had two sons, Habil and Qabil. Habil was kind and gentle. He looked after sheep and cows. Qabil was a farmer. He grew food on his farm. But Qabil was often jealous of his brother.

One day, the brothers had a big problem. Qabil was very angry. He said, “This is your end.” Habil said, “I will not hurt you. You are my brother, and I fear Allah.”

vocabulary.definition: Kind and quiet; does not hurt others.
Unhappy because someone has something good.
Be afraid of.

hotspots.title: Two Brothers
hotspots.description: Habil looked after sheep and cows. Qabil was a farmer.

hotspots.title: A Big Problem
hotspots.description: One day, the brothers had a big problem. Qabil was very angry.

exercises.title: Habil and Qabil
exercises.instructions: Match the name with the sentence.
exercises.question: Who did it?

matchingPairs.right: He looked after sheep and cows.
He grew food on his farm.

correctAnswer.Habil: He looked after sheep and cows.
correctAnswer.Qabil: He grew food on his farm.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 6 says: “He looked after sheep and cows. Qabil was a farmer. He grew food on his farm.”

feedback.correct: Yes! Habil looked after animals. Qabil was a farmer.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Look: Will Not
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the right answer.
languageFocusExercises.question: Habil said, “I will not hurt you.” What does this mean?
options: Habil is not going to hurt his brother.
Habil wants to hurt his brother.
languageFocusExercises.explanation: “Will not” + verb tells us about later. Habil is not going to do it.

feedback.correct: Yes. Will not = not later.
feedback.incorrect: Read Habil’s words at the end of Chapter 6.

languageFocusExercises.title: Practise: Habil or Qabil?
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Choose the right words.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who was it?

formChoices.sentence: Qabil was often [choice] of his brother.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: Habil was kind and gentle. Qabil was jealous. After “will not”, the verb has no -s.

feedback.correct: Correct.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 6 again.

languageFocusExercises.title: Write It: Two People
languageFocusExercises.instructions: Write about two people in your family.
languageFocusExercises.question: Who are they, and what do they do?

discussionPrompts.question: “My … is kind and …”
discussionPrompts.example: My sister is kind and gentle.

discussionPrompts.question: “My … is a … He / She …”

beforeYouRead.question: Guess first: Who was kind and gentle?

I can understand “will not”.
I can write about two people.

pages.title: The Crow
pages.content: But Qabil hit Habil with a stone, and Habil died. Then Qabil’s anger went away, and he felt very sad. He did not know what to do. Allah sent a crow. The crow made a hole in the soil. Qabil watched it and learned what to do with his brother’s body. He cried and said, “This crow knows more than me.” Then he went to another place. Adam was very sad. He said goodbye to his two sons on the same day. One went to a far country, and one died.

vocabulary.definition: A big black bird.
An open space in something.

feedback.correct: Correct. All three tell the past.

pages.title: Adam’s Message
pages.content:
Adam grew old. His children and their children took his message to every part of the world. The message is easy: Love Allah, be kind to people and do good things.

The story of Habil and Qabil also teaches us a lesson. Do not be jealous, and stop your anger. Allah is always with people. He never leaves them alone.

vocabulary.definition: A big black bird.
vocabulary.storyExample: Allah sent a crow.

vocabulary.definition: An open space in something.
vocabulary.storyExample: The crow made a hole in the soil.

vocabulary.definition: Words you send or tell to people.
vocabulary.storyExample: His children and their children took his message to every part of the world.

pages.title: Vocabulary Challenge
pages.content: Match six story words with their meanings.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: A being of light; it always does what Allah says.
vocabularyPairs.context: Then He told the angels about a new person.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: The brown ground; plants grow in it.
vocabularyPairs.context: The angels took soil from many parts of the earth.
Allah told Adam to be careful.
They knew it was a mistake.
Adam taught his children to be good and honest.

vocabularyPairs.meaning: Unhappy because someone has something good.
vocabularyPairs.context: But Qabil was often jealous of his brother.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review the language from all chapters.

exercises.title: Look: Two Kinds of Past
exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.
exercises.question: How does each verb show the past?
exercises.explanation: Many verbs add -ed: work → worked, help → helped. Some verbs change: make → made, take → took, eat → ate, give → gave.

feedback.correct: Well done. You found the two kinds of past.
feedback.incorrect: Say the verb today: work, make … Does it add -ed or change?

exercises.title: Practise: Was or Were
exercises.question: One or many?
exercises.explanation: One person: was. Two or more: were.

feedback.correct: Correct.
feedback.incorrect: Iblis = one. Adam and Eve = two.

exercises.title: Practise: Did Not
exercises.question: What did Iblis not do?
exercises.explanation: Did not + verb: did not show, did not say.

feedback.correct: Correct.
feedback.incorrect: After did not, the verb is like today: show, say.

exercises.title: Practise: Always, Often, Never
exercises.instructions: Fill the gaps with the words.
exercises.question: How often?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Iblis [blank] said sorry. Iblis [blank] thought he was right. Qabil was [blank] jealous of his brother.
exercises.explanation: Always = every time. Often = many times. Never = not one time.

feedback.correct: Correct.
feedback.incorrect: Find never, always and often in Chapters 4 and 6.

exercises.title: Practise: Fix One Word
exercises.instructions: Find the wrong word. Write the right word.
exercises.question: Can you fix the verb?

errorItems.sentence: Qabil growed food on his farm.

exercises.explanation: “Make” and “grow” change in the past: made, grew.

feedback.correct: Well done.
feedback.incorrect: Make → made. Grow → grew. They do not take -ed.

exercises.title: Use: A Good Day
exercises.instructions: Write three sentences about a good day.
exercises.question: What did you do on a good day?
exercises.explanation: Use one past verb, one because and one “Be …” sentence.

feedback.correct: Write three short sentences.

discussionPrompts.question: One past verb: “I helped …”
discussionPrompts.example: I helped my father.

discussionPrompts.question: One “because”: “I was happy because …”
discussionPrompts.example: I was happy because my friend came.

discussionPrompts.question: One “Be …”: a message for you
discussionPrompts.example: Be kind.

pages.title: Final Challenge
pages.content: Bring the whole story together in the Final Challenge.

exercises.title: The Father of All People
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence with one word: father, brother or son.
exercises.question: Who is Adam for all people?
exercises.fillBlanksText: Adam is the [blank] of all people.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 1: “Adam is the father of all people.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Adam is the father of all people.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 1.

exercises.title: Names
exercises.question: What did Allah teach Adam?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “Allah taught him the names of many things.”

feedback.correct: Yes. The names of many things.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Eve
exercises.question: Eve (Hawwa) was Adam’s wife.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “Allah gave him a wife. Her name was Eve (Hawwa).”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is true.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: A Big Lie
exercises.question: What was Iblis’s lie?
options: “Eat from that tree, and you will never die.”
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: Iblis said, “Eat from that tree, and you will never die.” It was a big lie.

feedback.correct: Yes. That was the lie.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 4.

exercises.title: Who Is It?
exercises.instructions: Match the name with the sentence.
exercises.question: Who is it?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: Eve was Adam’s wife. Chapter 6: “Habil was kind and gentle.” Chapter 4: Iblis “never said sorry”.

feedback.correct: Good. You matched all three.
feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 3, 4 and 6 again.

exercises.title: Life on Earth
exercises.question: Adam and Eve grew food on farms.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “They worked on farms and grew food.”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is true.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Habil’s Words
exercises.question: What did Habil say to Qabil?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 6: Habil said, “I will not hurt you. You are my brother, and I fear Allah.”

feedback.correct: Yes. Habil did not want to hurt his brother.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 6.

exercises.title: The Story of Adam
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Adam and Eve lived in Paradise.
Adam and Eve went to the earth.
Adam’s children took his message to the world.

exercises.explanation: Soil (Chapter 1) → Paradise (Chapter 3) → the earth (Chapter 5) → the message (Chapter 8).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the story of Adam.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
